paradigm: multi-paradigm - procedural, object-oriented, generic; compiled to native machine code

numeric_model.notes: no native arbitrary-precision/fixed-point decimal type in the core language; exact-precision arithmetic requires a library (e.g. Boost.Multiprecision) or a hand-written fixed-point type

exception_model: exceptions (try/catch/throw); commonly disabled entirely in embedded/performance-critical code, in which case error signaling reverts to return codes
concurrency_model: native OS threads (std::thread, since C++11); no GIL; manual synchronization via mutexes/atomics
native_sql_access: none in the standard library; requires a third-party driver (e.g. libpqxx, SOCI, ODBC)
multiple_inheritance_notes: native multiple inheritance, including virtual inheritance to resolve diamond-shaped hierarchies
notes: Drafted from general knowledge of the language, not yet checked by a project maintainer. Unlike Java/Python, C++ genuinely supports goto (inherited from C) - this is a real capability difference, not stylistic; it is simply discouraged in idiomatic modern C++. Verify every field before treating target-fit findings derived from this file as final.
